paragraphs.source_en: Thus one may quite well suppose that the structure of the human face can be called a memorial to God's successful creation, and at the same time regarded as a trace of failed creation. Of course, it may be all very well to think God omnipotent, but why should it not be equally acceptable to judge Him incompetent? These humans have both eyes set on the same plane, and can scarcely see left and right at the same time; therefore only one side of things enters their field of vision, which is precisely the pitiable part of being human. Put another way, a fact as simple as this occurs in their society day and night without interruption, yet because they themselves are dazed and overawed by God, they never come to understand it. If it is difficult to seek variety in manufacture, then it is equally difficult to manufacture a great many things that are exactly alike. If Raphael were asked to produce two Madonna paintings not differing by the smallest measure, or forced to paint two Marys with not the slightest resemblance to each other, either demand would be equally troublesome for Raphael. No, perhaps being asked to paint two completely identical pictures would be the more difficult task. To say to Kobo Daishi, “Please sign the two characters ‘Kukai’ in precisely yesterday's brush style,” might trouble him even more than asking him to change his calligraphic style entirely. The various languages humans use are handed down from generation to generation on a principle of pure imitation. When humans learn practical speech from their mothers, their nurses, or anyone else, they have not the slightest ambition beyond repeating the words they have heard; they merely imitate with all the ability they possess. That languages born of such imitation come, after ten or twenty years, to change in pronunciation proves that humans lack true powers of imitation. True imitation is as difficult as that. Consequently, when God created human beings, if He had been able to make them as though stamped from a single mold, so that one person could not be told from another, that would have truly proved His omnipotence; whereas exposing to broad daylight such a jumble of faces as we see today, producing variations enough to dazzle the eye, instead furnishes us with grounds for inferring God's incompetence.

In any case, when I caught sight of that gentleman of the beams opening the bedroom sliding door and suddenly appearing on the threshold, the reflections just given naturally welled up in my mind.
